chapter_name: Chapter 09: Tenses and Their Functional Uses
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will dive deep into advanced functional uses of tenses, focusing on Present Perfect vs. Simple Past, and understanding the Past Perfect and Future Perfect tenses.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Time traveling in English can get tricky! How do you talk about an action that started in the past but still matters today? Or something that will be finished by tomorrow? Let's upgrade our verb time-machines! 🚀

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Use Simple Past for a 'dead' action that finished at a specific time in the past. Use Present Perfect (has/have + 3rd form) for an action that happened in the past but has a RESULT or connection to the PRESENT. NEVER use Present Perfect with past time words like 'yesterday'.
examples_or_templates: Simple Past: I LOST my keys yesterday. (Action is totally in the past)
Present Perfect: I HAVE LOST my keys. (Result: I am standing outside my door right now, unable to get in!)

lesson_modules.module_title: ⏪ Past Perfect (The Past of the Past)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: When TWO actions happen in the past, one after the other, we use Past Perfect (had + 3rd form) for the FIRST action (the older one), and Simple Past for the SECOND action.
examples_or_templates: The train HAD LEFT before I REACHED the station.
(Action 1: Train left = Past Perfect. Action 2: I reached = Simple Past)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: We use the Future Perfect tense (will have + 3rd form) to talk about an action that will be COMPLETELY FINISHED before a certain time in the future. We often use it with 'by'.
examples_or_templates: By next year, I WILL HAVE GRADUATED from middle school.
She WILL HAVE FINISHED cooking by the time guests arrive.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct option: 'I _______ him yesterday.'
❓ Complete the sentence correctly: 'The patient _______ before the doctor arrived.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with Present Perfect or Simple Past: 'Oh no! I _______ (cut) my finger, and it is bleeding!'
subjective_practice.hint: Is there a result happening right now in the present?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Combine these using Past Perfect: 'I finished my homework. Then I went to play.'
subjective_practice.hint: Which action happened first? Make that one 'had + finished', and connect them with 'after'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a sentence using Future Perfect about something you will complete by 8:00 PM tonight.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🕰️ The Time-Traveler's Timeline
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Draw a timeline. On the left (Past), write 2 things you did yesterday. In the middle (Present connection), write 1 thing you 'have done' recently. On the right (Future), write 1 thing you 'will have completed' by next month!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Present Perfect connects a past action to a present result. Don't use it with past time markers like 'yesterday'.
⭐ Past Perfect is the 'past of the past'. It is used for the older action when two past actions happen.
⭐ Future Perfect describes an action that will be finished before a specific deadline in the future.
